expectations.text: Flags that the runbook never states who it is for or what the reader already knows
expectations.evidence: C1: 'The page never names its reader.'

expectations.text: Flags that the rollback procedure, the thing a reader of a runbook needs, is not at the top and is split across two sections
expectations.evidence: C2/C4 and S5/S7: the rollback answer is not first and is split across two sections.

expectations.text: Flags that the heading 'Rollback is automatic' contradicts its body, which describes a manual kubectl command
expectations.evidence: S2: '## Rollback is automatic' is followed by a manual kubectl step.

expectations.text: Flags that the processor timeout is stated as 30 seconds in one place and 60 seconds in others
expectations.evidence: S5/S6: the processor timeout appears three times with 30 and 60 seconds.

expectations.text: Flags that worker, consumer and job runner name the same component, or asks whether they are one component
expectations.evidence: L5: Architecture names three actors for one role.

expectations.text: Flags at least one pronoun ('it') whose antecedent is ambiguous
expectations.evidence: L1: 'it times out' and 'check this first' each have more than one antecedent.

expectations.text: Flags the 'in the YAML file, not in the Helm chart' contrast as unexplained or as implying an unstated rule
expectations.evidence: E2: 'set the retry count in the YAML file, not in the Helm chart' says the chart is wrong without saying why.

expectations.text: Flags writer-serving content: the 'This section will discuss' opener, the migration history, or 'It's worth noting'
expectations.evidence: S2 and L13: 'This section will discuss' and 'It's worth noting'.

expectations.text: Orders findings with reader/contract problems before structure problems before sentence-level problems
Gives a concrete rewrite for most findings, not only a description of the problem
expectations.evidence: Most findings carry a Rewrite block.
